## ⛔ RETRACTED by the filing seat — this card is wrong, and the mistake is a known, already-retracted one

Closing `not_planned` at 2026-09-22T02:46Z. ⛔ Nothing here needs doing.

**The card asserts four missed scheduled fires. There is no schedule to miss.** `.github/workflows/half-state-patrol.yml` on `origin/main` declares **no `schedule:` block at all**, and says so in its own `on:` comment:

> ⛔ ON DEMAND ONLY — this workflow declares NO schedule, and re-adding one takes the maintainer's sentence, not a reading of the history above. Ruling #208 on objectstack#19491, executed by objectstack#19497.

The retired schedule was `37 1,7,13,19 * * *` — exactly the cron this card quoted. It was removed **deliberately**, and the file records why: the patrol is report-only while the dispatch charter made its anchor rows a precondition for opening a dispatch, so a row misreading a now-legal state cost every executive seat a handling step four times a day. On the maintainer's question 「巡查仪留着却不继续开发,会不会反而不停的报错误的信息」 the answer measured yes. The ruling stops the clock, ⛔ not the instrument — the script stays runnable on `workflow_dispatch`.

So every symptom this card reported is the **designed** state: the last `event=schedule` run at 2026-09-21T01:56Z is the last one there will ever be, and the anchor's "expected every 6h · next by …" line is a deadline computed from constants that outlived the schedule they described. The file anticipates this reading too, and refuses it in advance: ⛔ "Do not re-add a `schedule:` block on the argument the history above makes."

## Why it was filed anyway — the instrument error, stated plainly

The seat read the **anchor's printed cron** and the **run history**, and concluded the fires were being dropped. It never read the workflow's own `on:` block, although it had the file open. That is reading the artefact an instrument printed instead of the instrument — the exact discipline this board enforces everywhere else, missed here.

⚠️ And it is not a novel error: **#19547 was this same mistake and is already retracted.** Filing it a second time is the more useful finding of the two, and it belongs to the seat rather than to the repo.

## What is NOT being claimed

⛔ No defect is asserted against the patrol, the anchor, or ruling #208. ⛔ No re-scheduling is proposed — that takes the maintainer's sentence by the file's own terms. The anchor's stale "next by" line is a known, documented consequence of the ruling and is out of scope here; if anyone judges it worth normalising, that is a separate card that must open by quoting ruling #208, ⛔ not by reporting a stall.

Retracted by the `domain:spec` execution seat, session `session_01UDXER3sdqfeVYpEWZs5mZx`. Re-opening is free if someone measures something this retraction gets wrong.
